about.title: Windsor Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Windsor sees a steady flow of traffic where Old Redwood Highway meets Shiloh Road and where US-101 cuts through town, and public crash records show 42 injury collisions and 54 people hurt in the most recent full year, with a spike in reports on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. Whether you were rear-ended near the Old Redwood Hw corridor or caught in a turning collision closer to town, the aftermath usually means medical appointments, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster who wants a recorded statement. We handle personal injury claims and represent you directly — meaning there's no fee unless you recover. Getting in touch early can help make sure evidence from the scene, witness accounts, and medical records don't get lost while decisions are still being made.
commonInjuries: Torn ligaments and soft tissue damage

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from a car accident to file a lawsuit, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a road maintained by the county — is involved. Contacting us sooner rather than later helps avoid missing a deadline that can't be undone.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Have to Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly blamed for a Windsor collision, you may still recover a share of damages. We can help make sure fault isn't overstated by an insurer looking to reduce a payout.

items.title: No Cap Doesn't Mean No Fight
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, but insurers still push back hard on these claims. Having representation before giving a recorded statement can help protect the value of what you've actually been through.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later, even if you're just trying to explain what happened. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: I was hurt near the Old Redwood Highway and Shiloh Road area — does that change anything?
items.answer: Not necessarily, but where a crash happens can affect which agency maintains the road and how evidence gets gathered, especially with corridors like Old Redwood Highway and US-101 seeing regular traffic in Windsor. We can look into road conditions, signal timing, or maintenance records if they're relevant to your case.

items.question: How much does it cost to get a case review?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer free case reviews, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
